sentence: This project studies the ethical, legal and social implications of genetics and genomics.
This project uses a biodegradable material called acetalated dextran to deliver an immune-activating drug to the tumor site after glioblastoma surgery.
This project studies how DNA replication and chromatin assembly create asymmetries in cell division during development and in germline stem cells.
This project studies how lipid nanoparticles deliver gene editing to specific tissues such as the liver, lung and spleen.
This project studies the costs and effects of consultants used by nonprofit health care organizations in the US health system.
This project builds and tests a family-centered model for cancer risk communication for children with genetic cancer risk.
This project develops a treatment for triple-negative breast cancer that uses targeted therapies derived from sharks to deliver radionuclides to the tumor.
This project builds a digital tool that uses speech recordings and machine learning to help diagnose frontotemporal dementia.
This project tests gene editing as a therapy for cerebral small vessel disease, using a genetic vasculopathy model.
This project uses mutagenesis to build a database of mutations that make Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to the antibiotic bedaquiline.
This project studies how an attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant that produces a tryptophan metabolite changes the tumor microenvironment and immunotherapy resistance in melanoma.
This project studies how a small molecule activates Piezo ion channels and designs molecules that change how these channels work.
This project uses molecular imaging to measure a growth factor receptor and blood vessels in breast cancer that has spread to the brain.
This project studies what causes blood clots in cancer patients treated with immunotherapy, using patient samples and a mouse model.
This project studies whether esophageal adenocarcinoma and intestinal gastric cancer arise from a common cell-of-origin.
This project tries to find out which gene regulation programs drive metastatic outgrowth of breast cancer cells.
This project uses zebrafish to study how mucosal epithelial cells build microridges, protrusions that help retain mucus.
This project studies how human cells stop Toxoplasma growth and how the parasite counteracts this.
This project builds a CRISPR screening platform to find genes that control phagocytosis in microglia in Alzheimer's disease.
